steps.note: Create the event that will first be checked in the vendor portal Live tab.
Give the live event a known title for vendor-portal verification.
Apply the pricing template required before adding line items.
Add one product so the event can be published.
Complete the pricing sheet before scheduling and publishing.
Commit a valid bidding schedule.
Invite the QA vendor whose portal view is being tested.
Publish the event so it appears as open or upcoming to the vendor.
Confirm the event reached a published project page.
Open the vendor portal in a separate session while keeping the buyer session available.
Open the vendor portal's Live view.
Assert that the Live view is present.
Verify the open event is visible to the vendor in Live.
Return to the buyer session to create historical-state events.

steps.note: Move the first event into a closed historical state.

Create a separate event that will be withdrawn.
Give the withdrawn event a known title.
Apply the required pricing template.
Add the required product.
Complete the pricing sheet.
Commit the event schedule.
Invite the vendor to the withdrawn event.
Publish the event before withdrawing it.
Confirm the withdrawn candidate was published.
Move the second event into the withdrawn historical state.
Confirm Procol records the project as withdrawn.
Create a separate event that will be awarded.
Give the awarded event a known title.
Apply the required pricing template.
Add the product to be awarded.
Complete the pricing sheet.
Commit the event schedule.
Invite the vendor to the awarded event.
Publish the event so it can receive a bid.
Confirm the awarded candidate was published.
